size.description: Returns the current size (number of entries) of the permanent chain. This represents how many state snapshots have been committed.

resolve.description: Returns committed/indexed content for a specific path. Optional pinned? and proof? flags control whether local pin status and serialized proof material are included.

resolve-batch.description: Resolves up to 1,024 ordered committed paths from one request. Paths may span local and federated route/history groups; compact proofs are verified internally, duplicates remain ordered, and optional pinned? status is origin-local.
resolve-batch.example: ((function resolve-batch) (arguments ((paths ((-1 *state* alice key) (-1 peer-a -1 *state* bob key))) (pinned? #t) (expression? #t))) (authentication ((identity (*state* alice)) (credentials "mysecret"))))

trace.description: Returns a serialized traced object for a committed path at a specific chain index. Used by bridges and remote synchronization helpers.

trace-batch.description: Returns one compact serialized union proof for up to 1,024 authorized paths sharing one history anchor. Heterogeneous anchors require separate calls or resolve-batch grouping.

info.description: Returns public config info about this journal, including the public key and window size. Used by bridges to identify and verify this journal.

get.description: Retrieves data from the current staging area only. Use resolve for committed/indexed reads.

get-batch.description: Reads up to 1,024 ordered staged paths from one snapshot. Duplicate and missing paths remain in request order; expression? controls value decoding.
get-batch.example: ((function get-batch) (arguments ((paths ((*state* alice one) (*state* alice missing))) (expression? #t))) (authentication ((identity (*state* alice)) (credentials "mysecret"))))

set!.description: Sets a staged value. Optional expected content makes the write conditional: mismatch returns #f without mutation and requires both get and set! authority.

call!.description: Interface loads the current staged Scheme procedure once for a configured administrator/root, evaluates it outside sync-let in a masked environment, and applies it to the only authenticated journal capability followed by the explicit arguments list. Authorization rules and namespace ownership cannot grant it; execution is local-only and non-atomic.

pin!.description: Pins data at the specified path to prevent it from being pruned. The path must include a chain index as the first element. Pinned data is preserved in the permanent chain.

pin-batch!.description: Atomically pins up to 1,024 complete origin-relative committed paths. Remote proof groups are fetched and verified before the one local retention mutation; any failed member rolls back all retention changes.
pin-batch!.example: ((function pin-batch!) (arguments ((paths ((-1 *state* alice important-data) (-1 peer-a -1 *state* bob shared))))) (authentication ((identity (*state* alice)) (credentials "mysecret"))))

unpin!.description: Unpins data at the specified path, allowing it to be pruned. The path must include a chain index as the first element.

unpin-batch!.description: Atomically removes retained proof material for up to 1,024 complete origin-relative paths. Duplicate and overlapping cuts are idempotent; malformed members roll back the batch.
unpin-batch!.example: ((function unpin-batch!) (arguments ((paths ((-1 *state* alice old-data) (-1 peer-a -1 *state* bob old-data))))) (authentication ((identity (*state* alice)) (credentials "mysecret"))))

config.description: Returns the full config of the ledger, including both public and private settings.

bridge!.description: Creates a reciprocal bridge and takes responsibility for initiating synchronization.

update-config!.description: Updates a ledger configuration path. Used for bridge acceptance and preapproval settings.

*secret*.description: Rotates the journal-wide Interface authentication secret and corresponding Interface public signing key. Configured local Interface administrators/root only.

set-batch!.description: Atomically stages multiple path/value writes. Optional expected values are checked against one snapshot; any mismatch returns #f without mutation and requires get plus set! authority for every path.
set-batch!.example: ((function set-batch!) (arguments ((paths ((*state* alice one) (*state* alice two))) (values (1 2)) (expected (0 1)) (expression? #t))) (authentication ((identity (*state* alice)) (credentials "mysecret"))))

delete-bridge!.description: Deletes a local reciprocal bridge and its alias-scoped authorization state. Configured local Interface administrators/root only.

authorizations.description: Lists exact authorization rules owned by a local (*state* USER) namespace. Owners may list their own rules; Interface administrators/root may manage local namespaces.

authorize!.description: Adds an exact owner-local rule. Remote principals require terminal authentication key-index; Resolve has a separate document-history range. Exact local/public rules omit key-index.

deauthorize!.description: Deletes an owner-local authorization rule using the complete exact stored shape, including key-index and Resolve range.

*admins-get*.description: Returns configured local Interface administrator principals. Interface administrators/root only.

*admins-set*.description: Replaces configured local Interface administrator principals. Every entry must be exact (*state* USER). Interface administrators/root only.

*window-set*.description: Sets the positive ledger retention window. Interface administrators/root only; decreasing may prune unpinned history.

*eval*.description: Evaluates an arbitrary Scheme expression with full access to the journal internals. Extremely powerful and dangerous - use with caution.

*call*.description: Calls a function with the root object as an argument. The function receives direct access to the root data structure.

*step*.description: Executes a full step cycle: by default it refreshes configured bridges, commits the current staged state, and returns the new chain size. An optional query can drive a custom installed step handler operation.

*set-secret*.description: Changes the admin secret used for root-level operations. Requires the current admin secret for authentication.

*set-step*.description: Sets the step handler function that is called during *step* operations. The function receives the root object, admin secret, and optional step query.

*set-query*.description: Sets the query handler function that processes all incoming queries. The function receives the root object and query data.
